title: Akrou residents protest prefect’s interim village-chief appointment
location: Akrou, Jacqueville department; residents blocked the Jacqueville–Abidjan road.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending: KOACI and Yessouan confirm a gathering and blockade but give no simultaneous participant count or clearly supported qualitative >=50 estimate. Search-only APA text has mass language but a related opened page is AP/APA credited and origin-ambiguous; AbidjanTV uses “marée humaine” but has unresolved date/provenance. Those claims are not used to meet the threshold.

start_date.summary: Both reports locate the protest on 18 October 2024.

location.summary: Akrou/Jacqueville; road from Jacqueville toward Abidjan was blocked.

demands.summary: Residents contested the prefect’s interim-chief appointment and sought cancellation/suspension and to address the prefect.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Reports say security forces used tear gas to disperse the gathering.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither body gives a participant number or clearly supported size wording; threshold unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: No participant violence can be determined from the captured descriptions; barricades alone do not establish violence.

notes: APA follow-up and AbidjanTV pages were opened but are not used for claims: the APA body credits “AP/APA,” while AbidjanTV has undated/stale metadata and poor page quality. Yessouan separately mentions 2021 protests; its 2021 counts and arrests are excluded from this 2024 candidate. No automatic episode merge with prior village disputes.
open_questions: Can a credible, permitted account establish >=50 participants present simultaneously on 18 October?
Is there an independent contemporaneous account with a reliable headcount or qualitative threshold description?
What precise remedy did protesters demand from the prefect and did any state accommodation or arrests occur on 18 October?
Did any new gathering occur in November, or is the November reporting only retrospective follow-up?
